title: Compromising the Intelligence of Modern DNNs: On the Effectiveness of Targeted RowPress
problem: RowPress attacks can flip targeted bits in DRAM similar to RowHammer; impact on deep neural networks unexplored. Existing RowHammer mitigation mechanisms are ineffective against RowPress, creating a new DNN vulnerability.
motivation: DNN security and robustness; understanding emerging DRAM attack vectors is critical for securing AI systems in shared computing environments.
method: The researchers develop an attack methodology by profiling Samsung DRAM chips to capture how RowPress (a memory-based attack that flips targeted bits through repeated access patterns) produces distinct bit-flip patterns compared to RowHammer. They then evaluate how these RowPress-induced bit-flips affect 11 different neural network architectures across multiple standard benchmark datasets to measure the real-world impact.
key_novelty: This is the first comprehensive evaluation showing that RowPress attacks degrade deep neural networks faster than RowHammer attacks.
contributions: First evaluation of RowPress attack impact on DNN systems
DRAM-profile-aware attack methodology for pattern analysis
Demonstration that RowPress causes faster DNN performance degradation than RowHammer
Evidence that existing RowHammer mitigations are ineffective against RowPress

metrics.other: RowPress causes faster performance degradation than RowHammer

limitations: Evaluation limited to single DRAM manufacturer (Samsung); vulnerability characteristics and mitigation effectiveness for other vendors unclear.
primary_theme: RowPress DRAM attack vulnerability in deep neural networks
